newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican trains collide head-on injuring 40.
newsitem.headline: Mexican trains collide head-on injuring 40.

text.p: Two Mexican trains collided head-on at slow speeds on Monday in the south of the western state of Jalisco, injuring 40 passengers, the Jalisco state Red Cross said.
"In total the report has 40 injuries from moderate to light," Edgar Aguilar, the Red Cross's chief of radio communications in Jalisco, told Reuters. "Nobody has died as of the moment."

Jalisco state authorities said a passenger train and a cargo train, both belonging to the state-owned Ferrocarriles Nacionales de Mexico, met head-on at the small town of Tlajomulco de Zuniga because of "a lack of coordination," according to Carlos Barragan, chief of the state's Civil Protection Guard.
